items.title: How much does a decision's stakes and reversibility change how much depth it actually needs?
items.description: Priya's sync-interval call was high-stakes and only medium-reversible, which pushed it toward real care rather than a quick skim. Drag stakes and reversibility to see how much personal depth (in hours of self-study, versus relying on a checked expert conversation) a decision like hers would actually warrant, on top of the roughly one hour a well-run expert conversation takes regardless.

params.name: reversibilityLevel
params.label: Reversibility (0 = hard to undo, 10 = trivially reversible)

items.compute: const risk = params.stakesLevel * (10 - params.reversibilityLevel); const depthHoursWarranted = Math.round((risk / 100) * 120 * 10) / 10; return { depthHoursWarranted };

outputs.label: Personal depth warranted beyond a checked expert conversation

items.title: How much does a slow time-to-signal raise the real cost of a wrong call, before it's caught?
items.description: Priya's mobile call was risky partly because battery drain wouldn't surface for weeks, letting a mistake keep compounding the whole time. Assume a wrong call causes a fixed amount of harm per day it goes undetected. Drag how many days it would take a wrong call to surface (a fast-failing crash near 0, gradual battery drain near 30+) to see how much total damage accumulates before anyone catches it — this is exactly why a canary rollout, which shortens detection time, is the lever Priya reaches for.

params.name: daysToSignal
params.label: Days until a wrong call would surface on its own

items.compute: const harmPerDay = 40; const totalHarm = params.daysToSignal * harmPerDay; return { accumulatedHarm: totalHarm };
